sentenceSets.sentence: Ignoring the injury only aggravated it; by week's end he could barely walk.

answerChoices.reasoning: Worsened means made worse, nearly synonymous with aggravated, but is more neutral and doesn't emphasize the intensifying effect.
Exacerbated means made more severe, very close to aggravated, but is more formal and emphasizes intensity.
Intensified means made stronger or more acute, close to aggravated, but doesn't specifically convey harm or damage.
Escalated means increased in severity, but doesn't specifically convey injury damage or deterioration.
Inflamed relates to physical inflammation, fitting injury, but doesn't convey the worsening from ignoring it.
Irritated means annoyed or made sore, but is less severe than the injury worsening implied by aggravated.
Increased means made larger, but doesn't specifically convey harm or deterioration of the injury.
Prolonged means extended in time, fitting the ongoing damage, but doesn't emphasize the worsening.
Improved means made better; aggravated means made worse—opposite effects.
Healed means recovered; aggravating an injury prevents healing—opposite outcomes.
Resolved means settled or cured; aggravated means worsened—opposite effects.

sentenceSets.sentence: The drought aggravated the famine, pushing millions to the brink of starvation.

answerChoices.reasoning: Deepened means made more severe, fitting the worsening famine, but doesn't convey the causal intensification that aggravated does.
Compounded means made more complex or severe, close to aggravated, but is broader and doesn't emphasize intensification.
Amplified means increased in effect, but doesn't convey the worsening relationship between drought and famine.
Worsened means made worse, fitting the effect, but doesn't convey the causal relationship that aggravated implies.
Prolonged means extended in time, which the drought might do, but doesn't emphasize the intensification.
Intensified means made stronger, but doesn't specifically convey the cause-effect relationship.
Contributed to means helped cause, but is less emphatic about making worse than aggravated.
Exacerbated means made more severe, close to aggravated, but emphasizes severity rather than causing intensification.
Relieved means eased or alleviated; aggravated means intensified—opposite effects.
Resolved means solved; the drought aggravates famine, making it worse—opposite effects.
Halted means stopped; aggravated means intensified—opposite effects.

sentenceSets.sentence: The student's repeated lateness aggravated the teacher's frustration, nearly testing her patience to its limit.

answerChoices.reasoning: Increased means made greater, fitting the growth of frustration, but doesn't convey the sense of worsening or intensifying.
Deepened means intensified, fitting the worsening frustration, but doesn't convey the cumulative effect of repeated actions.
Compounded means made more complex or serious, but doesn't specifically convey the worsening of frustration.
Heightened means increased in intensity, close to aggravated, but doesn't emphasize the incremental building effect.
Fueled means supplied with fuel or encouraged, but doesn't specifically convey worsening of feelings.
Triggered means caused to activate, but doesn't convey the ongoing worsening that aggravated implies.
Provoked means stirred to action or anger, but doesn't convey the sense of worsening over time.
Strained means put pressure on, but doesn't specifically convey the cumulative worsening of frustration.
Soothed means calmed; aggravated means intensified—opposite effects.
Resolved means solved; the lateness aggravates frustration, making it worse—opposite effects.
Eased means made easier or less severe; aggravated means made worse—opposite effects.
